title: FREE WAND
subtitle: Draw the grimoire in the air.
lead:
Pick up the wand and you are a magician.
Draw one of the nine spells written in the grimoire, and the world in the mirror catches fire, floods, and is swept through by wind.
shiftNote: * The demo is not running at every hour of the day.
c1: In the mirror, the world lets magic through
c1lead: ne large mirror stands at the booth. What it shows is not another world — it is the very place you are standing in. The difference is that in there, magic has somewhere to go. And only the person holding the wand can open that road.

c1items.b: There is only one wand at the booth. When someone sets it down, the next person picks it up. While you hold it, you are the only magician in the room.
The spells are written in the grimoire: three for fire, three for water, three for wind. Open a page, learn the shape, and draw that shape in the air.
A spell you managed to draw is always answered. What burns is the reality on screen itself — no background is ever swapped in for another world.

c1note: What is free is how you stand and how you draw. The wand knows its own movement, so there is no mark on the floor to stand on. Stand where you like, face where you like, draw at any size. The grimoire fixes the shape, and nothing else.
c2lead: Three for fire, three for water, three for wind. Every mark is drawn in a single stroke. Neither size nor tilt is ever asked of you — only the shape is written here.

fire.name: Fire
fire.read: The marks of fire all have corners. Drawn in one breath, the arrow turns back sharply at its tip.

items.name: Sparks
items.body: One arrow, straight up. Embers lift away trailing tails of fire

items.name: Pillar
items.body: An inverted mark beneath the arrow. A tongue of flame climbs, wavering

items.name: Vortex
items.body: A great triangle laid over the mark. Three flames spiral as they rise

water.name: Water
water.read: The marks of water have no corners. However the stroke bends is how the water will behave.

items.name: Droplet
items.body: Close the line. From the point where it lands, a ring of spray opens out

items.name: Wave
items.body: Repeat the same sway. Water runs left and right, and floods the floor

items.name: Whirl
items.body: Wind inward from the outside. Arms take hold of the image and drag it under

wind.name: Wind
wind.read: The marks of wind are lines that keep turning. Wind does not go where you drew it; it goes to whoever is standing there.

items.name: Slash
items.body: One open arc. It winds around the person, then unwinds and cuts

items.name: Updraft
items.body: Gather low, spring up. It rises from the feet and carries the person with it

items.name: Ring
items.body: Cross the line and bring it back. A ring lies flat and keeps turning — the wind that stays longest

c3lead: Once you know the shape, only four movements remain. Nothing is posted at the booth: the tremble of the wand and the colour of the light tell you what comes next.

steps.b: Turn a slow circle with the tip. Power begins to gather
steps.alt: Drawing a circle with the wand

steps.b: When the wand trembles, you are full
The mark you learned, straight into the air
Bring it down when you are done. The mark is let go

c3note: The mark is drawn into the light at the foot of the screen, and leaves from there for the world. The magic comes out where the light is, not where you drew. To start again, lower the wand along your body.
c3quote: Not one word appears during the rite. No score, no gauge, no READY. The tremble of the wand and the colour of the light are the only things that tell you where you are.
c4lead: All the wand says is how it moved. What happens next is always decided on the mirror’s side.
figCap: Between the wand and the mirror

c4items.b: The wand knows where it is from its own movement. Neither the lighting of the hall nor where you stand can throw it off — which is why there is no mark taped to the floor.
The size of the flame and the speed of the wind can be changed while it runs, over and over. How it looks is only settled once we are in the hall.
Feed in a stroke recorded once, and the same judgement runs with no wand in the room. The nine marks were settled by redrawing them a few hundred times that way.

c5lead: Press enquiries, exhibition proposals and technical questions are all welcome. We answer within a few days.
fBodyPh: Press enquiry, a joint exhibit, a question about the build…
